abstract: Although the 2015 National Institutes of Health mandate to consider sex as a biological variable in preclinical studies has increased sex-inclusive study designs, many research groups continue to cite the complexity of monitoring female-specific physiology as a barrier to adoption. Central to this challenge is the murine estrous cycle, a hormonally driven process comprising four stages (proestrus, estrus, metestrus, and diestrus), each associated with distinct hormonal and cytological profiles. Current staging methods rely primarily on vaginal cytology, which requires skilled animal handling, specialized expertise in cytology observation, and considerable time, limiting their routine application outside of reproductive endocrinology. To address these barriers, we developed and evaluated a machine learning framework for estrous cycle staging based on photographs of the mouse external vaginal opening. Using 2,297 photographs from C57BL/6J and BALB/c female mice paired with concurrent cytological assessments and partitioned strictly at the animal level, we trained and evaluated three models of varying granularity: a four-stage model, a three-stage model combining metestrus and diestrus, and a two-stage binary model separating the follicular from the luteal and transitional phases. In a held-out evaluation cohort of 466 photographs from 29 unseen mice, overall classification accuracy was 47.4% (95% CI: 40.7-51.9%) for the four-stage model, 54.5% (47.6-62.9%) for the three-group model, and 69.5% (61.8-75.3%) for the binary two-group model. Misclassifications occurred predominantly between biologically adjacent stages, particularly between proestrus and estrus. Crucially, applying a calibrated confidence threshold to the two-group classifier increased accuracy to 82.8% (95% CI: 71.1-92.1%) among the 43.8% of photographs with confidence [≥] 0.80, and to 92.5% (95% CI: 87.1-96.6%) among the 20.0% of photographs with confidence [≥] 0.90. While external photography does not support standalone four-stage classification, confidence-guided photographic assessment offers an accessible decision-support framework to selectively triage uncertain cases for cytology and reduce the wet-lab burden of estrous monitoring in preclinical research, including cohort assembly for hormone-dependent models of genital tract infection.
